rationale:
The parent-supplied proof combines two separate, reusable obligations. Each becomes a child.

(1) covector_space_finite_dimensional (parent step 6): Λ^n(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n is finite-dimensional. This is pure linear algebra. Mathlib does not provide it as an instance in this contract: `infer_instance` fails for both `FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n)` and `Module.Finite`. The fact is reusable wherever a basis of the covector space, or its separability, is needed.

(2) orient_component_vanishes_ae (parent steps 1–5, for a single covector α): the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations applied to the scalar component ξ(·)(α) with respect to the weight μ = θH^n⌞M. This is the analytic core. It proves the bound |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ directly from IsUnitOrientationOf, so it needs no sibling or uncle dependency.

The two children are independent, so there are no sibling edges.

After the split the parent keeps only its short assembly (its own steps 1, 7 and 8):
- (a) By R.orients, μ ≪ H^n⌞M and the accepted sibling `imsupp_unit_orientation_ne_zero_norm_le_one` (already a resolved dependency of this node), ξ(x) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. x.
- (b) By child 1 fix a basis α_1,…,α_N := Module.finBasis.
- (c) Apply child 2 to each α_k and combine with ae_all_iff over Fin N: for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ W implies ξ(x)(α_k) = 0 for all k.
- (d) For such an x in W, ξ(x) vanishes on a basis, so ξ(x) = 0 (Basis.ext). This contradicts (a). So μ-a.e. x lies outside W, and μ(W) = 0 (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem).

So the children together with the accepted sibling imply exactly the selected statement. Neither child restates the parent or solves another DAG node.

subproblems.title: The space of n-covectors on ℝ^P is finite-dimensional
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. The real vector space Λ^n(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with its standard ℝ-module structure, is finite-dimensional over ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent-supplied proof (finite-dimensionality of Λ^n via injective evaluation on tuples of basis vectors).
Notation: E := ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). Λ^n := Covector E n = E [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ, the continuous alternating n-linear forms on E, with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication.

1. Basis. Let e = (e_1,…,e_P) be the standard basis of E (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ, viewed as a Module.Basis indexed by Fin P).

2. Evaluation map. Define L : Λ^n → ((Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ) by L(α)(I) := α(e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(n)}) = α(e ∘ I) for each index map I : Fin n → Fin P. For fixed I, α ↦ α(e ∘ I) is additive and ℝ-homogeneous, because (α + β)(v) = α(v) + β(v) and (cα)(v) = c·α(v). So L is ℝ-linear.

3. Injectivity. Suppose L(α) = L(β). Then α(e ∘ v) = β(e ∘ v) for every map v : Fin n → Fin P, in particular for every injective v. An alternating n-linear map on a module with basis e is determined by its values on the tuples e ∘ v with v injective (Module.Basis.ext_alternating). So the underlying alternating maps of α and β coincide. A continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). Hence α = β, and L is injective.

4. Conclusion. The codomain (Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ ≅ ℝ^{P^n} is a finite-dimensional real vector space, since its index type Fin n → Fin P is finite. A vector space with an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective, applied to L and step 3). Therefore Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n is finite-dimensional over ℝ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix the standard basis e of ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (EuclideanSpace.basisFun).
Define the ℝ-linear map L(α) = (α(e ∘ I))_{I : Fin n → Fin P} into the finite-dimensional space (Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ.
L is injective: Module.Basis.ext_alternating identifies the underlying alternating maps, and ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective identifies the continuous ones.
FiniteDimensional.of_injective gives FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n).

subproblems.title: Where a represented current vanishes on an open set, each scalar component of its orientation vanishes weight-a.e. (fundamental lemma)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P, let T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Suppose W is open, W ⊆ U, and T vanishes on W (T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W). Then for every n-covector α ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n, for R.measure-almost every x: if x ∈ W then ξ(x)(α) = 0. Here R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, x ∈ W → R.orient x α = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–5 of the parent-supplied proof, which proves the consequence 'T vanishes on W ⇒ μ_T(W) = 0' of Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–768); Simon states it without proof. Here the argument is specialized to one covector α. The norm bound of parent step 1 is proved inline, so no other lemma is needed.
Notation: M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient. ν := H^n⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M. μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity(x ↦ (θ(x) : [0,∞])). Fix α ∈ Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n and put f(x) := ξ(x)(α) ∈ ℝ.

1. Absolute continuity. μ is a withDensity measure of ν, so μ ≪ ν (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). Hence every property that holds ν-a.e. also holds μ-a.e. (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le).

2. Pointwise bound. By R.orients, for ν-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. That is, there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1,…,τ_n) in ℝ^P such that either ξ(x)(β) = β(τ) for every β, or ξ(x)(β) = −β(τ) for every β. In either case |f(x)| = |α(τ)|. By the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖, since each ‖τ_i‖ = 1 by orthonormality. So |f(x)| ≤ ‖α‖ for ν-a.e. x, hence for μ-a.e. x by step 1.

3. Measurability. ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient). Evaluation L ↦ L(α) is a continuous map MultiVector P n → ℝ (continuous_eval_const). So f = (L ↦ L(α)) ∘ ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable). By step 1 it is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac), and hence also a.e. strongly measurable for every restriction μ⌞K.

4. Finiteness on compact subsets of U. Let K ⊆ U be compact. K is closed in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence Borel measurable. By withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict,
 μ(K) = ∫⁻_{x∈K} θ(x) dν(x) = ∫⁻_{x ∈ K∩M} θ(x) dH^n(x) = ∫⁻_{x ∈ M∩K} θ(x) dH^n(x).
 This is finite by R.locallyIntegrable_mult, applied to the compact set K with K ⊆ U. So μ(K) < ∞.

5. Local integrability on W. W is open, hence locally closed, and ℝ^P is locally compact. By locallyIntegrableOn_iff it suffices to show that f is integrable on every compact K ⊆ W. For such K we have K ⊆ W ⊆ U, so μ(K) < ∞ by step 4. Also f is μ⌞K-a.e. strongly measurable by step 3, and |f| ≤ ‖α‖ holds μ⌞K-a.e. by step 2 (ae_restrict_of_ae). Hence f is integrable on K (IntegrableOn.of_bound). So f is locally integrable on W with respect to μ.

6. Test forms supported in W. Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W. Define ω(y) := g(y)·α.
 - ω is C^∞, being the product of the smooth scalar function g with the constant α (ContDiff.smul with contDiff_const).
 - ω has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
 - tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left).
 Hence ω ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport ω ⊆ W, so T(ω) = 0 because T vanishes on W. By R.Represents T,
 0 = T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_{x∈M} θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)·α) dH^n(x).

7. Rewriting the integral against μ. θ is ℕ-valued and measurable. The density of μ is x ↦ (θ(x) : [0,∞]), which equals x ↦ ((θ(x) : ℝ≥0) : [0,∞]) because the coercions ℕ → [0,∞] and ℕ → ℝ≥0 → [0,∞] agree. The map x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ≥0) is measurable (measurable_from_nat composed with R.measurable_mult). Mathlib's integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul, which needs no integrability hypothesis, gives
 ∫ g(x)·f(x) dμ(x) = ∫ (θ(x) : ℝ≥0)·(g(x)·f(x)) dν(x) = ∫_{x∈M} θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)·α) dH^n(x).
 The last equality holds pointwise: (θ(x) : ℝ≥0)·r = (θ(x) : ℝ)·r, and ξ(x)(g(x)·α) = g(x)·ξ(x)(α) by linearity of ξ(x). By step 6 the right-hand side is 0. So ∫ g(x)·f(x) dμ(x) = 0 for every C^∞ compactly supported g with tsupport g ⊆ W.

8. Fundamental lemma. ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space with its Borel σ-algebra, and ℝ is complete. Apply the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations on an open set (Mathlib IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero) to the measure μ, the open set W and the function f. Its hypotheses are local integrability of f on W (step 5) and the identity of step 7 for all smooth compactly supported g with tsupport g ⊆ W. It requires no local finiteness of μ. Hence for μ-a.e. x: x ∈ W ⇒ f(x) = ξ(x)(α) = 0, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ = R.measure is absolutely continuous with respect to ν = H^n⌞M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous).
R.orients and ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm with orthonormal τ give |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ ν-a.e., hence μ-a.e.
f = ξ(·)(α) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: continuous evaluation composed with the a.e. strongly measurable ξ, then mono_ac.
μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, R.locallyIntegrable_mult).
f is locally integrable on the open set W (locallyIntegrableOn_iff and IntegrableOn.of_bound).
For smooth compactly supported g with tsupport g ⊆ W, ω = g·α ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W, so 0 = T(ω) = R.action(ω).
integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul and linearity of ξ(x) give ∫ g·f dμ = R.action(g·α) = 0.
